approaches.name: statewide flood early warning and emergency operations system
approaches.description: The project builds an end-to-end flood early warning system with geospatial analytics, 72-hour forecasts, embankment monitoring and upgraded emergency operations centers issuing geotagged alerts. Practices: flash flood forecasting program piloted in Phase 2 and scaled in Phase 3; state EOC upgraded to fusion center with district EOCs; flash flood forecasting program with EWDS dissemination; upgraded FLEWS with 72-hour lead time and 2-D inundation models; real-time embankment monitoring feeding early warning system; geospatial analytics EWDS with geotagged multi-channel alerts; GIS-based village disaster mitigation plans with monitoring system; FLEWS upgrade with river and floodplain inundation forecasts; end-to-end EWDS with geospatial analytics and EOC management system.

extra_evidence.text: Piloting Flash Flood Forecasting Scaling Up Flash Flood Forecasting Studies Water Resources Beki and Buridehing Basin no Investments in Beki, Buridehing, and Investments in 5 more Basins based on Infrastructure regret investments Jiadhal Basins based on Integrated Flood IFRMP Component 2: Risk Management Plan (IFRMP) Water Flood Forecasting Flood Forecasting & IFRMP for Flood Forecasting and IFRMPs for 5 more Flood Forecasting for Brahmaputra Resources & IFRMPs Beki, Buridehing, Jiadhal Basins Basins Mainstem Management Embankment Asset Formulation of Asset Piloting Asset Management Program Scaling Up Asset Management Program Management Management Program Implementation Implementation Pilot upgrading of school flood Scaling-up upgrading of school flood relief Scaling-up upgrading of school flood Flood Shelters relief shelters and new flood shelters and new flood shelters (75 relief shelters and new flood shelters (75 shelters (25 shelters) shelters) shelters) Upgrading State and Select Upgrading of State EOC to Fusion Center Establish EOCs for 30% of the Revenue Early Warning and District Emergency Operations and additional District EOCs Circles (55 circles) Component 3:
In Phase 1, ASDMA will undertake a “flash flood forecasting study” to design a state-wide program that will allow for earlier and more accurate warnings.
The flash flood forecasting program will be piloted in Phase 2 and scaled up in Phase 3.
The flash flood warnings will be disseminated through ASDMA’s upgraded Early Warning and Dissemination System (EWDS) in Component 3.

In parallel with the IFRMPs, the existing Assam Flood Early Warning System (FLEWS) will be upgraded by increasing the lead time for flood forecasting from 24 hours to 72 hours and expanding the scope to include both river overflows and floodplain inundation (using a combination of 1-D and 2-D models, and other flood prediction tools).
Currently, the North Eastern Space Applications Centre (NESAC) is generating the flood forecasts which are then provided to ASDMA for early warning dissemination.
In addition, it will provide real-time monitoring of flood embankment status during the monsoon season which will then feed into ASDMA’s EWDS.
An EWDS will be developed across Assam that is supported by intelligent geospatial analytics and an Emergency Operations Center (EOC) management system.
The EWDS will be able to provide real-time geotagged alerts to multiple locations simultaneously using a variety of communication channels, including the cell network.
In Phase 1, the State EOC will be upgraded and new EOCs will be established in at least 10 districts.
The VDMPs will use a combination of risk analysis processes, including participatory community-based analysis, site surveys, and development of GIS-based risk maps.
A climate resilient village monitoring system will be developed by ASDMA that tracks progress over time according to standardized criteria.
This component will also upgrade the existing Assam FLEWS by increasing forecasting lead times and include both river and floodplain inundation forecasts.
WRD’s HIU, in collaboration with NESAC, will be responsible for flood forecasting and ASDMA will provide early warning through the upgraded EWDS described in Component 3.
Component 3.2: Early Warning and Dissemination System (US$10 million).
Support for an end-to-end EWDS across Assam to be supported by geospatial analytics and an EOC management system, including: (i) upgrading EOCs at the state level and in selected districts;
(ii) providing geo-referenced alerts using cell-phone broadcasting; and (iii) establishing a geospatial laboratory.
